title: BIS Ten-Touchpoint Instructional Standard
purpose: Make the ten-touchpoint programme a deliberate learning progression in which concepts are discovered, explained, applied, investigated, reviewed and transferred, and in which every meaningful learner action has a defined evidence/reporting job.

invariantProgrammeModel.learnerShift: From ordinary experience to a problem worth investigating.
From noticing to a first usable distinction or model.
From classroom model to a personal investigation question, prediction and safe plan.
invariantProgrammeModel.boundary: The 45-minute learning session prepares the handover. Live Lab Phase A remains a separate facilitated experience and is not collapsed into this session.

invariantProgrammeModel.learnerShift: From what the Lab surfaced to formal language that explains the learner's own evidence.
From general framework to a personal, evidence-linked working model.
From plan to observation in authentic context.
From result to diagnosis, barrier analysis and justified adjustment.
From local technique to a broader conceptual layer that increases range.
From one investigated pattern to a second context and an integrated explanation.
From completed programme to evidenced progress, limits, next practice and transfer forward.
invariantProgrammeModel.boundary: Day 10 is not another theory chapter.

fortyFiveMinuteGrammar.purpose: Recover prior learning/evidence without reteaching the lesson.
Create a dilemma, prediction, comparison, demonstration or evidence encounter.
Name only the concepts needed to make sense of the discovery.
Use a discriminating learning check, not a recall-for-recall quiz.
Move from worked example to guided or personal application.
Work with traceable evidence, a prediction, plan, observation or governed task.
State what the evidence supports and what it does not yet support.
Define the precise observation/action that makes tomorrow possible.

discoveryRule.statement: Do not reveal a formal explanatory model before the learner has encountered enough of the phenomenon for the explanation to mean something.
allowedBeforeDiscovery: definitions required to understand the task
disallowedBeforeDiscovery: the answer the investigation is designed to reveal
a finished interpretation presented as the learner's conclusion

requirements: Every learner-facing question has a downstream job.
Pre/post comparisons use the same construct, task family or explicitly comparable measure.
Prediction, plan, simulation, observation, outcome, interpretation and transfer remain distinct.
A reflection is not an observed outcome.
A completed lesson is not evidence of competency.
The highest competency progression level is constrained by evidence type, provenance and context.

dailyAcceptanceCriteria: Knowledge change: what does the learner understand at minute 45 that was not available at minute 0?
Capability change: what can the learner now do, explain, test or review?
Evidence contribution: what traceable item, if any, was created and what can it support?
Reporting contribution: which report classification may use that evidence and under what boundary?
Carry-forward dependency: what must happen between this touchpoint and the next?
facilitatorRole: Create conditions for discovery rather than read the handbook aloud.
Name concepts only when the learner has something meaningful to attach them to.
Protect evidence integrity and separate observation from interpretation.
Help the learner state uncertainty and limits.
Use private learner content only within authorised boundaries.
